newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia one-mth interbank up after intervention.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia one-mth interbank up after intervention.

text.p: One-month interbank rate rose by 10 basis points to 7.15/20 percent immediately after Bank Negara's intervention in the domestic money market to borrow for a one-month deposit, dealers said on Friday.
They said while the volume of Bank Negara's intervention was not known, it certainly gave a psychological boost to rates, which were threatening to fall below the central bank's support levels.
One-week money rose to 6.40/50 percent from 6.30/40, and two-week to 6.50/60 from 6.40/50.
Three-month money at 7.20/25 percent and six-month at 7.25/30 were unchanged from their Thursday levels.
Dealers said Bank Negara probably decided to intervene in the money market after interbank rates resumed their decline on fresh inflow of funds.
The fresh inflow was largely from the maturity of a Bank Negara intervention deposit.
The central bank came in later than its usual intervention time to raise a one-month deposit at a steady 7.05 percent.
Bank Negara regularly intervenes in the interbank money market to keep a check on liquidity or set interest rates as part of its inflation fighting efforts.
Political uncertainties in the region have been also been attracting funds to Malaysia through swaps, dealers said.
"There is too much short-term money in the market. It would have sent the wrong message out about the monetary policy," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
He said it was clear that these short-term funds were not likely to participate in the series of large issues next week which could absorb the liquidity.
It was to pull out these funds that Bank Negara came into the market, he said.
"If they had not done it today, there is another maturity of a Bank Negara deposit on Monday," said Jimmy Koh, analyst with research firm I.D.E.A in Singapore.
"Bank Negara had to show it still has a grip on the monetary policy," he added.
Bank Negara is issuing a two billion ringgit seven-year Malaysian government bond and Cagamas is planning a notes and a bond issue for 550 million ringgit next week.
